[Thinking]
**Creating CPI Table**

I'm considering how to compute the changes in YoY core CPI (Consumer Price Index) from published monthly percent change data. It sounds like a good plan to say, "Here are the YoY core CPI changes (CPI-U less food and energy)," and include a table. I want to clarify that these values represent annual percent changes. I can use known official data from 2015 and 2016, and I need to double-check those January values for accuracy while rounding to one decimal point.
[/Thinking]

Here’s the U.S. **core inflation rate** (YoY change in **CPI less food and energy**, rounded to 1 decimal) from **Jan 2015 to Dec 2016**:

| Month | YoY core inflation |
|---|---:|
| 2015-01 | 1.6% |
| 2015-02 | 1.7% |
| 2015-03 | 1.8% |
| 2015-04 | 1.8% |
| 2015-05 | 1.7% |
| 2015-06 | 1.7% |
| 2015-07 | 1.8% |
| 2015-08 | 1.9% |
| 2015-09 | 1.9% |
| 2015-10 | 2.0% |
| 2015-11 | 2.0% |
| 2015-12 | 2.1% |
| 2016-01 | 2.2% |
| 2016-02 | 2.3% |
| 2016-03 | 2.2% |
| 2016-04 | 2.1% |
| 2016-05 | 2.2% |
| 2016-06 | 2.3% |
| 2016-07 | 2.2% |
| 2016-08 | 2.3% |
| 2016-09 | 2.2% |
| 2016-10 | 2.1% |
| 2016-11 | 2.1% |
| 2016-12 | 2.2% |

If you want, I can also provide this as a CSV or plot it as a chart.
